questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to extend behavior without touching core dispatch logic; demonstrates the Command pattern with a runtime registry.

## Key Concepts
- Command pattern
- Registry-based extensibility
- Safe, non-invasive extension

## Code Example
```javascript
interface Command { execute(args: string[]): void; }
class Registry { private map = new Map<string, Command>(); register(name: string, c: Command) { this.map.set(name, c); } get(name: string): Command | undefined { return this.map.get(name); } }
class Router { constructor(private registry: Registry) {} route(argv: string[]) { const cmd = argv[0]; const command = this.registry.get(cmd); if (command) command.execute(argv.slice(1)); else throw new Error('Unknown command'); } }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle asynchronous commands? 
- How would you ensure thread-safety in a multi-process CLI?

## Why This Is Asked
Introduce a new angle: runtime-extensible evaluation logic for feature flags to reflect real-world needs in large orgs.

## Key Concepts
- Strategy pattern for evaluators
- Registry for dynamic extension
- Composite rule composition (anyOf/allOf)

```typescript
type EvalContext = { user: any; time: Date; attrs: any }

  register(name: string, factory: (cfg: any)=>Evaluator): void

}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How to model evaluation order and short-circuit semantics?
- How to handle cross-feature conflicts and auditing of evaluator registrations?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question tests ability to build a safe, extensible plugin pipeline for high-throughput payments, focusing on runtime extensibility, isolation, and concurrency control.

## Key Concepts

- Pipeline pattern
- Registry/plugin system
- Stateless processors
- Per-event isolation
- Concurrency and backpressure

## Code Example

```typescript
interface Event { id: string; payload: any }
interface Processor { process(e: Event): Promise<Event> }
type Factory = () => Processor
class Registry { register(name: string, f: Factory): void; create(name: string): Processor | null }
```

```
// Minimal usage
const reg = new Registry()
reg.register('audit', () => new AuditProcessor())
reg.register('enrich', () => new EnrichProcessor())
reg.register('risk-check', () => new RiskCheckProcessor())

async function handleEvent(e: Event) {
  const names = ['audit', 'enrich', 'risk-check']
  const pipeline = names.map(n => reg.create(n)!).filter(Boolean)
  let ev = e
  for (const p of pipeline) {
    ev = await p.process(ev)
  }
  return ev
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you enforce per-event isolation if processors mutate payload in place?
- What strategies would you use to implement backpressure when the registry contains many heavy processors?
